previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: James, a man with a history of COPD, alcohol use disorder, chronic pain, and tobacco use, was admitted for hypoxia and acute alcohol intoxication. He presented with shortness of breath, wheezing, and slurred speech, and was found at a train stop. He was treated for COPD exacerbation with prednisone, nebulizers, and levofloxacin, and for alcohol withdrawal with valium and supportive vitamins. His chest X-ray showed bibasilar atelectasis with a right lower lobe opacity concerning for infection. Laboratory results revealed initial leukopenia, hypomagnesemia, and hypernatremia, all of which improved with treatment. He expressed interest in entering a recovery program and was close to securing a placement, but eloped from the hospital at 5:30 AM on hospital day two, before completing detox or receiving discharge instructions.

ASSESSMENT & PLAN:  
___ year old male with EtOH abuse, COPD presenting with COPD 
exacerbation, CXR concerning for PNA.

# PNA vs. COPD exacerbation: CXR is concerning for a pneumonia 
and patient is diffusely wheezing with cough.  Patient with 
crepitus on the right and also with diffuse wheezing.  He is 
coughing although not bringing up much sputum.  He is without a 
leukocytosis although symptoms still concerning.  He was started 
on prednisone 40mg PO Daily, clindamycin 300mg IV Q8H and then 
transitioned to PO after 24 hours and a z-pack.  After 24 hours, 
he was satting well on room air.  His exam had also improved 
after 24 hours of therapy.  He continued to do well and will 
complete a 5 day course of prednisone, 5 day course of 
azithromycin and 7 day course of clindamycin.  He was discharged 
on tiotropium Daily and albuterol rescue inhaler.  He will need 
outpatient follow up with PFTs. He left AMA.

# EtOH Intoxication: Patient has long history of alcoholism.  He 
started drinking when he was ___ years old and has been drinking 
since then.  His longest duration of abstinence was ___ years, 
but he relapsed after the death of his sons.  He has lost a lot 
of his loved ones and his other living son is in prison.  He 
continues to leave AMA, likely to keep drinking.  He was 
determined to stay on this admission.  He initially required 
15mg of valium every 2 hours, but slowly his withdrawal symptoms 
improved and his daily requirement of valium decreased.  He 
scored less on the CIWA scale and eventually left AMA.

# HTN: Patient was hypertensive that ranged in the systolics 
from 150s to 190s.  Hard to tell how much of this was his benign 
essential HTN and how much is from alcohol withdrawal.  He was 
started on his home enalapril and metoprolol and BPs improved.  
It's unclear if he is taking enalapril and metoprolol at home 
because he always leaves AMA and does not refill scripts.

# Atypicals on Diff: Unclear etiology.  He does not have a 
leukocytosis and may be secondary to alcohol effects on the 
marrow vs. viral process vs. malignancy.  Needs  work up as an 
outpatient.  

# Narcotics seeking: History of narcotics seeking behavoir, left 
AMA when he did not get narotics on last admission.  He was not 
given narcotics on this admission.
